entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen35571" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen35572" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen35573" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen35573" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen35572" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen35574" type="x-p"/> In thus chapter God promises the continuance of his favor to those who are returned from the captivity; so that upon the removal of his judgments, the fasts they had observed during the captivity may now be converted to so many occasions of rejoicing. He likewise promises in due time a general restoration of his people, and the enlargement of the Church by the accession of the Gentiles, vv. 1-20. The conclusion of the chapter intimates farther that the Jews, after their restoration, will be instrumental in converting many other nations, <reference osisRef="Zac.8.21-Zac.8.23">Zac 8:21-23</reference>. Compare <reference osisRef="Rom.11.15">Rom 11:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.11.16">Rom 11:16</reference>.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen35574" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35575" type="x-p"/> I was jealous - Some refer this to the Jews themselves. They were as the spouse of Jehovah: but they were unfaithful, and God punished them as an injured husband might be expected to punish an unfaithful wife. Others apply it to the enemies of the Jews. Though I gave them a commission to afflict you, yet they exceeded their commission: I will therefore deal with them in fury - in vindictive justice.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen35575" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35576" type="x-p"/> I am returned unto Zion - I have restored her from her captivity. I will dwell among them. The temple shall be rebuilt, and so shall Jerusalem; and instead of being false, unholy, and profligate, it shall be the city of truth. and my holy mountain. Truth shall dwell in it.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen35577" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35578" type="x-p"/> The streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls - The progeny shall be numerous, healthy, and happy. Their innocent gambols and useful exercises shall be a means of health, and a proof of happiness. To be healthy, children must have exercise. But they cannot take exercise, except in the way of play and diversion: ergo, such playfulness cannot be sinful. Let them be kept from evil words, lying, swearing, and scurrility; and all the rest may be innocent.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen35583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35584" type="x-p"/> As ye were a curse - Instead of being execrated among the people, ye shall be blessed; instead of being reproached, ye shall be commended. entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 19</hi> <div eID="gen35586" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35587" type="x-p"/> The fast of the fourth month - To commemorate the taking of Jerusalem; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.3">2Kgs 25:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.39.2">Jer 39:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.52.6">Jer 52:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.52.7">Jer 52:7</reference>. <div eID="gen35587" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35588" type="x-p"/> The fast of the fifth - In memory of the ruin of the temple, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.8">2Kgs 25:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.52.12">Jer 52:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.52.13">Jer 52:13</reference>. <div eID="gen35588" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35589" type="x-p"/> The fast of the seventh - For the murder of Gedaliah, Jeremiah 41:1-17. <div eID="gen35589" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35590" type="x-p"/> The fast of the tenth - In commemoration of the siege of Jerusalem, which began on the tenth day of the tenth month; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.25.1">2Kgs 25:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.52.4">Jer 52:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eze.24.1">Eze 24:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eze.24.2">Eze 24:2</reference>; and see on <reference osisRef="Zac.7.3">Zac 7:3</reference> (note), <reference osisRef="Zac.7.5">Zac 7:5</reference> (note). <div eID="gen35590" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35591" type="x-p"/> Cheerful feasts - Ye shall find all your evils so completely redressed, that these mournful fasts shall be turned into joyful feasts.
entries.content_plain: Verse 19 The fast of the fourth month - To commemorate the taking of Jerusalem; 2Kgs 25:3 ; Jer 39:2 ; Jer 52:6 , Jer 52:7 . The fast of the fifth - In memory of the ruin of the temple, 2Kgs 25:8 ; Jer 52:12 , Jer 52:13 . The fast of the seventh - For the murder of Gedaliah, Jeremiah 41:1-17. The fast of the tenth - In commemoration of the siege of Jerusalem, which began on the tenth day of the tenth month; 2Kgs 25:1 ; Jer 52:4 ; Eze 24:1 , Eze 24:2 ; and see on Zac 7:3 (note), Zac 7:5 (note). Cheerful feasts - Ye shall find all your evils so completely redressed, that these mournful fasts shall be turned into joyful feasts.

Many Gentiles, as well as Jews, will then be found devoting themselves to the Lord.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 23</hi> <div eID="gen35594" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35595" type="x-p"/> Ten men - shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew - The converts from among the Gentiles shall be to the Jews as ten to one. But ten may here signify a great number, without comparison. And from this scripture it appears as if the Jews, converted to God, should be the instruments of converting many Gentiles. See on <reference osisRef="Isa.3.6">Isa 3:6</reference> (note). Catching hold of the skirt is a gesture naturally used to entreat assistance and protection. This and the three foregoing verses, says Abp. Newcome, refer to the great accession of converts which the Jewish Church received between the captivity and the coming of Christ; to the number of Christian disciples which the Jewish preachers made, and to the future conversions of which the restoration of the Jews will be an eminent cause.  <chapter eID="Zech.8"/> <div eID="gen35595" type="x-p"/>
